verdict.rationale: Ramp documents a policy layer of funds with amount, interval, merchant-category, merchant and country restrictions, plus role- and amount-based workflows. It also shows in-policy expenses being auto-approved while risky items escalate to a human. This covers the core of the story, but role-based limits and the configuration of auto-approval rules are only implied by marketing copy and an example scenario. missing for 10: documented per-role spend limits (role appears only in notification/routing workflows), first-party docs on configuring auto-approve thresholds and exception routing for expenses, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can codify our expense policy — limits by category, role, and context — so in-policy expenses auto-approve and only exceptions reach a human

citations.quote: Funds. A budget with restrictions — amount, interval (daily, monthly, total), allowed merchant categories, allowed merchants, allowed countries.
Set submission requirements, enforce spend limits, and block risky merchants or categories all before spend happens.
Create personalized workflows that only notify the right people, based on spend amount or team role, and keep visibility high.
the receipt is captured automatically, coded to the correct GL account, and auto-approved because it's within policy — no expense report filed
Approves when it's safe. Escalates when it's not
